docs.title: Seismic Interpretation
docs.text: Seismic facies classification and horizon picking automation.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This machine learning system is part of the Oil & Gas ML Portfolio by Kelvin J Cabrera.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Synthetic Data Generator -> Scikit-Learn Training -> Flask API -> Streamlit Dashboard

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Data Generation: Domain-aware synthetic data with physical correlations
  • Model Training: Scikit-learn pipelines (Random Forest, Isolation Forest) with MLflow tracking
  • API: Flask/FastAPI with API key authentication
  • Dashboard: Streamlit interactive web interface
  • Testing: pytest with model evaluation metrics (R2, accuracy, F1)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt
python train.py
python app.py
streamlit run streamlit_app.py

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Endpoint Description GET / Service info and available models POST /predict/{model} Run inference (requires API key)

Authentication

All API endpoints require an X-API-Key header. Set API_KEY in your environment.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require an API key sent via the X-API-Key header.

import requests

headers = {"X-API-Key": "your-api-key"}
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5000/predict/model", json={...}, headers=headers)

docs.title: GET /
docs.text:
Returns service information and available models.

Response:

{"service": "Seismic Interpretation", "models": ["model1", "model2"]}

docs.title: POST /predict/{model_name}
docs.text:
Run inference on a trained model.

Request Body:

{"features": {"feature_1": 0.5, "feature_2": 1.2}}

Response:

{"prediction": 0.85, "model": "model_name"}

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 Invalid or missing API key 404 Model not found 422 Invalid input format

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
• Source: Synthetic data generator (generate_synthetic_data)
  • Samples: 2,000 seismic attribute records
  • Features: amplitude, frequency, phase, acoustic_impedance, velocity, density
  • Targets: porosity_prediction (regression), lithology_prediction (classification)

docs.title: HorizonTracker
docs.text:
• Algorithm: GradientBoostingRegressor (n_estimators=200, max_depth=5)
  • Task: Predict porosity from seismic attributes
  • Input: 6 scaled seismic features
  • Output: Porosity value (continuous)
  • Serialization: pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: FaciesClassifier
docs.text:
• Algorithm: RandomForestClassifier (n_estimators=200, max_depth=12)
  • Task: Classify lithology facies from seismic attributes
  • Input: 6 scaled seismic features
  • Output: Facies label (integer) + probability distribution
  • Serialization: pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: Preprocessing Pipeline
docs.text:
• StandardScaler for all 6 features
  • Single scaler shared between both models
  • Saved as scaler.pkl

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text:
• Framework: Flask
  • Port: 5013
  • Format: JSON request/response
  • Endpoints: 5 (track, classify, health, models, docs)

docs.title: Dashboard Layer
docs.text:
• Frontend: HTML/CSS/JS (Jinja2 templates)
  • Charts: Chart.js for visualization
  • Theme: Dark theme UI

docs.title: Horizon Tracking Flow
docs.text:
1. User provides array of seismic feature objects
  2. Features extracted in predefined column order
  3. StandardScaler transforms features
  4. GradientBoostingRegressor predicts porosity per sample
  5. Array of porosity predictions returned

docs.title: Facies Classification Flow
docs.text:
1. User provides array of seismic feature objects
  2. Features extracted and scaled
  3. RandomForestClassifier predicts facies label + probabilities
  4. Labels and probability distributions returned

docs.title: Feature Processing
docs.text:
All features are standardized (zero mean, unit variance) using StandardScaler:

Feature Unit Physical Meaning amplitude - Reflection strength at interface frequency Hz Spectral content of wavelet phase radians Wavelet phase characteristic acoustic_impedance kg/m2s Rock acoustic property velocity m/s Seismic wave speed density g/cm3 Rock bulk density

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
FROM python:3.9-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

RUN python train.py

EXPOSE 5013

CMD ["python", "app.py"]

docs.title: Build and Run
docs.text:
docker build -t seismic-interpretation .
docker run -p 5013:5013 seismic-interpretation

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
version: '3.8'
services:
  seismic-interpretation:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "5013:5013"
    environment:
      - FLASK_ENV=production
    volumes:
      - model-data:/app/outputs

volumes:
  model-data:

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default FLASK_ENV Flask environment mode development PORT Server port 5013

docs.title: Production Considerations
docs.text:
• Use gunicorn for production serving: bash gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:5013 app:app
  • Set debug=False in app.py (already set)
  • Configure reverse proxy (nginx) for SSL termination
  • Set up health check monitoring on /api/health
  • Use a process manager (systemd, supervisor) for auto-restart

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
1. python train.py generates synthetic seismic data
  2. StandardScaler fitted on features
  3. Models trained and evaluated
  4. Artifacts saved to outputs/models/:
  5. horizon_tracker.pkl - Porosity predictor
  6. facies_classifier.pkl - Lithology classifier
  7. scaler.pkl - Feature scaler
  8. metadata.json - Training summary

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml): - Runs on push to main - Installs dependencies - Runs training pipeline - Executes API tests

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Seismic Interpretation system uses machine learning for horizon tracking (porosity prediction) and facies classification from seismic attributes. It provides a REST API and web dashboard for real-time seismic data analysis.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • pip

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
cd seismic-interpretation
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Train Models
docs.text:
python train.py

This generates 2,000 synthetic seismic samples and trains: - HorizonTracker (GradientBoostingRegressor) - Predicts porosity from seismic attributes - FaciesClassifier (RandomForestClassifier) - Classifies lithology from seismic attributes

docs.title: Run the Server
docs.text:
python app.py

Open http://localhost:5013 in your browser.

docs.title: Dashboard Features
docs.text:
• Horizon Tracking Panel - Input seismic attributes to predict porosity
  • Facies Classification Panel - Input seismic attributes to classify rock type
  • Model Metrics - View training accuracy, R2 scores, and feature importances
  • Chart.js Visualizations - Visual analysis of prediction results
  • Dark Theme UI - Modern dark-themed dashboard

docs.title: Horizon Tracking (Python)
docs.text:
import requests

response = requests.post("http://localhost:5013/api/track", json={
    "features": [
        {
            "amplitude": 0.5,
            "frequency": 30,
            "phase": 0.0,
            "acoustic_impedance": 2000,
            "velocity": 2500,
            "density": 2.2
        }
    ]
})
result = response.json()
print(f"Porosity prediction: {result['predictions'][0]:.4f}")

docs.title: Batch Processing
docs.text:
Both /api/track and /api/classify support batch processing by passing multiple feature objects in the features array:

import requests

response = requests.post("http://localhost:5013/api/track", json={
    "features": [
        {"amplitude": 0.5, "frequency": 30, "phase": 0.0, "acoustic_impedance": 2000, "velocity": 2500, "density": 2.2},
        {"amplitude": -0.3, "frequency": 45, "phase": 1.5, "acoustic_impedance": 1800, "velocity": 2200, "density": 2.0},
        {"amplitude": 0.8, "frequency": 35, "phase": 0.5, "acoustic_impedance": 2200, "velocity": 2800, "density": 2.4},
    ]
})
results = response.json()
for pred in results['predictions']:
    print(f"Porosity: {pred:.4f}")

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Models not loaded: Run python train.py first
  • Missing features error: All 6 seismic attributes are required per feature object
  • Port in use: Change port in app.py

Elaborado por Ing. Kelvin Cabrera

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
The training pipeline follows these steps:

  1. Data Generation: data_generator.py creates synthetic data with domain-specific physical correlations
  2. Preprocessing: Feature scaling via StandardScaler
  3. Training: Random Forest or Isolation Forest via scikit-learn
  4. Evaluation: R2 score, accuracy, classification report
  5. Logging: MLflow tracks parameters, metrics, and artifacts
  6. Serialization: Model + scaler + metadata saved as .pkl via joblib

docs.title: Model Files
docs.text:
Models are stored in outputs/models/*.pkl as dictionaries with:

Key Description model Trained scikit-learn estimator scaler Fitted StandardScaler feature_names List of input feature names target_name Target variable name metrics Evaluation metrics from training

docs.title: Retraining
docs.text:
To retrain:

python train.py

This will update the model files in outputs/models/ and log results to MLflow.
